newsitem.title: ITALY: Europe's new car market rises 9.2 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Europe's new car market rises 9.2 pct in April.

text.p: The European new car market rose 9.2 percent to 1,258,200 units in April, helped by a large rise in Italian new car registrations, said Italian vehicle makers association Anfia in a statement on Friday.
Without the rise in Italian April registrations of 52.37 percent, the European new car market ex-Italy in April would have shown a rise of only 2.6 percent.

In the first four months of 1997, European new car registrations showed a rise of 0.6 percent to 4,654,500 from the same period in 1996. Without Italy, the market would have showed a 3.6 percent fall.
In April, new car registrations rose 1.3 percent in Germany, Britain was up 11.8 percent and Spain up 19.2 percent, while the fall in French sales continued, off 10 percent in April.
In the first four months, new car sales in France fell 22.6 percent and in Germany off 3.9 percent. Britain and Spain showed a rise of 5.4 percent and 9.3 percent respectively.
